newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 25.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- The Economic and Social Research Institute has urged the government to consider adding a tax on new mortgages and tightening lending regulations to curb rising home prices

- Irish Tycoon Ben Dunne gave the Fine Gael party 185,000 pounds over a four-year period, making him the party's largest single donor in recent years, the party's secretary general told the payments-to-politicians tribunal.

- Michael Smurfit, head of the Jefferson Smurfit group, has urged the government to do its utmost to ensure that Ireland does not become a two-tier society with only some sections enjoying the fruits of economic success.
- The Economic and Social Research Institute has urged the government to considering taxing new mortgages to stop property prices and housing debit spiralling.
- Hospital and health services face complete shutdown after a decision by 10,000 health workers to ballot for industrial action in support of 3,000 striking paramedics.

- New doubts arose last night about whether former government minister Michael Lowry will give evidence to the payments-to-politicians inquiry before a general election. There is intense speculation that the Tribunal will adjourn early next week.
- The Prime Minister and other government leaders have decided to put back the date for the general election until June to enable important legislation to be put through parliament.

- Rural Ireland is set to reap a jobs bonus from European companies disenchanted by the business climate in Eastern Europe, the head of the government's Industrial Development Agency (IDA), Kieran McGowan, said on Thursday.
